title: The Real Notice
intro: An email from Zelvora. After tonight, you might be ready to call everything a scam.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

notify.text: We're updating our app on Friday

subject.text: IMPORTANT: We're updating our app on Friday

p: On Friday we're releasing Zelvora 4.2 with faster swaps.

p.text: Update from your phone's official app store when it appears.

p: There's nothing else you need to do.

p.text: Reminder: Zelvora staff will never message you first or ask for your recovery phrase.

noreply.label: no-reply address
noreply.lens: Sent from no-reply@zelvora.app, Zelvora's real domain.
noreply.why: Companies often send from no-reply addresses. The domain is the official one.

subject.label: IMPORTANT in caps
subject.lens: Capital letters, but no deadline, no threat.
subject.why: Shouting alone isn't a scam sign. Threats and deadlines are.

name.label: Uses your name
name.why: Real companies know your name. (Scammers can too, so it proves nothing on its own.)

update.label: Asks you to update
update.lens: It sends you to the official app store. No link to click.
update.why: Pointing you to the official store, not a link, is what honest companies do.

reminder.label: Safety reminder
reminder.lens: It repeats the Golden Rule from your first case.
reminder.why: Real companies warn you about scams.

actions.label: Update from the app store when it appears

go_ahead.line: Friday came, the update arrived in the app store, and swaps got faster. Nothing to fear.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. It was a real notice, and the app updated itself on Friday.

block_report.line: That was the real Zelvora. When every message looks like a scam, the real warnings get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: Nothing in it asked for money, codes, a phrase or a link. That calm is what real messages look like.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asked for nothing secret.

golden_rule: Real messages ask for nothing secret and point you to the official app, not a link.

quick_check.q: What showed this email was genuine?

options.text: It asked for nothing and pointed to the official app store

quick_check.explain: Names, times and footers can all be copied. Asking for nothing secret, and no link to click, is the real sign.

hints.nudge: What is this email actually asking you to do?

kit.label: Check links
kit.title: What the email asks you to click

rows.v: None. It points to the app store
